questions.title: Hi-Q Tyre Invoice and Tyre Insurance — Reading a Financial Document and a Graph

subQuestions.questionText: Ms R. Gumede received a Hi-Q financial document dated 21/12/2021 with a due date of 31/12/2021. Write down the due date of this financial document.
subQuestions.memoText:
31/12/2021 (31 December 2021)

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: The document is headed 'INVOICE: 6359', lists quantities, descriptions, unit prices, VAT and a TOTAL DUE. Name the type of financial document shown.
subQuestions.memoText:
An invoice (or tax invoice).

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: State two ways of contacting Hi-Q, using the information on the document (Phone: 021 851 7124; Email: hiqswest@gmail.com; address: 61 Victoria Road, Somerset West).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any two of: by phone (021 851 7124); by email (hiqswest@gmail.com); in person at the address (61 Victoria Road, Somerset West).

[Award 2 marks — 1 per method]

subQuestions.questionText: Give the name and address of the customer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Ms R. Gumede, 17 Mountain Road, Somerset West, 7130.

Mark 1: name (R. Gumede)
Mark 2: address (17 Mountain Road, Somerset West, 7130)

subQuestions.label: 1.1.5 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: State the total VAT amount payable for this transaction.
subQuestions.memoText:
R271,30

[Award 2 marks for reading the TOTAL VAT line]

subQuestions.label: 1.1.5 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Give the name of the bank that Hi-Q banks with.
subQuestions.memoText:
Nedbank

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.label: 1.1.5 (c)
subQuestions.questionText: What does the acronym VAT stand for?
subQuestions.memoText:
Value-Added Tax

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: The document shows 2 tyres for a combined total of R1 780 (including VAT). State the unit price, including VAT, of the Falken tyres.
subQuestions.memoText:
Unit price = R1 780 ÷ 2 = R890

Mark 1: dividing by 2
Mark 2: answer R890

subQuestions.questionText: Write as a unit ratio (to two decimal places) the total price of the tyres (R1 780) to the price of the wheel alignment (R300), in the form 1 : ______.
subQuestions.memoText:
R1 780 : R300
Divide both by 1 780
= 1 : 0,17

Mark 1: R1 780 : R300
Mark 2: dividing both by 1 780 → 1 : 0,17

subQuestions.questionText: A 'Time-Based Credit Matrix' graph shows the percentage credit a customer receives against the age of the tyre in 3-month bands: 0–3 months 84%; 3–6 months 68%; 6–9 months 52%; 9–12 months 52%; 12–15 months 36%; 15–18 months 36%; 18–21 months 20%; 21–24 months 10%. Name the type of graph illustrated.
subQuestions.memoText:
A histogram (bar graph).

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Write down the maximum benefit amount per tyre.
subQuestions.memoText:
R6 000 per tyre (including VAT)

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: State the maximum number of months for this insurance cover.
subQuestions.memoText:
24 months (valid for two years)

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: When will a customer not enjoy any insurance benefit within the insurance period?
subQuestions.memoText:
When the tyre has less than 2 mm of tread (regardless of the age of the tyre) — the credit is then 0%.

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: If the tyres were 14 months old, what percentage credit would R. Gumede receive? (Assume she has not paid the top-up amount.)
subQuestions.memoText:
14 months falls in the 12–15 month band → 36%

Mark 1: identifying the 12–15 month band
Mark 2: 36%

subQuestions.label: 1.2.6 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: The TopUp TyreSurance costs a once-off 20% of the tyre value. R. Gumede bought 2 tyres with a combined value of R1 780. Determine the cost to TopUp her TyreSurance for all the tyres she bought.
subQuestions.memoText:
TopUp cost = 20% × R1 780 = R356

Mark 1: 20% of R1 780
Mark 2: answer R356

subQuestions.label: 1.2.6 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Using the given information, state the benefit of paying for this TopUp TyreSurance.
subQuestions.memoText:
She gets 100% cover for 24 months (two years), instead of the reducing time-based percentage credit.

[Award 2 marks]

questions.title: Dewald Brevis — Cricket Statistics, Currency Conversion, Bar Graphs and Shares

subQuestions.label: 2.1.1 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: Dewald Brevis scored: 65 vs India; 104 vs Uganda; 96 vs Ireland; 97 vs England; 6 vs Sri Lanka; 138 vs Bangladesh. Calculate Brevis's mean number of runs scored.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mean = (65 + 104 + 96 + 97 + 6 + 138) ÷ 6 = 506 ÷ 6 = 84,33 (accept 84)

Mark 1: adding the six scores
Mark 2: ÷ 6 → 84,33

subQuestions.label: 2.1.1 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine his median number of runs scored.
subQuestions.memoText:
Ordered: 6; 65; 96; 97; 104; 138
Median = (96 + 97) ÷ 2 = 96,5 (accept 96 or 97)

Mark 1: ordering the data
Mark 2: median = 96,5

subQuestions.label: 2.1.1 (c)
subQuestions.questionText: Calculate his range of runs scored.
subQuestions.memoText:
Range = 138 − 6 = 132

Mark 1: max − min
Mark 2: answer 132

subQuestions.questionText: Brevis's IPL contract was valued at 3 Indian crore. Calculate the value of his contract in South African rand, and write your final answer in words without using any number values. Use: 1 Indian crore = 10 million Indian rupees; 1 rupee = R0,20.
subQuestions.memoText:
Number of rupees = 3 × 10 000 000 = 30 000 000 rupees
Rand value = 30 000 000 × R0,20 = R6 000 000
In words: six million rand.

Mark 1: 3 × 10 000 000
Mark 2: 30 000 000 rupees
Mark 3: × 0,20
Mark 4: R6 000 000
Mark 5: 'six million rand'

subQuestions.label: 2.1.3 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: The table shows base prices and contract prices (in crore) for 2022 IPL contracts: Kagiso Rabada 2 / 9,25; Faf du Plessis 2 / 7; Quinton de Kock 2 / 6,75; Marco Jansen 0,5 / 4,2; Dewald Brevis 0,2 / 3. Draw an appropriate graph showing the base price and contract price for each player. Describe the graph you would draw (heading, axis labels, key).
subQuestions.memoText:
A double (compound) bar graph.
Heading: e.g. "South African Cricketers' Contract Prices for IPL 2022".
Horizontal axis: South African cricketers. Vertical axis: Amount in Crore.
Key: Base Price / Contract Price.
Two bars per player, drawn to the values in the table, with a space between each player's pair.

Mark 1: heading, axis labels and legend
Mark 2: double bar graph form
Marks 3–4: first three players' bars plotted correctly (base + contract)
Marks 5–6: last two players' bars plotted correctly
Mark 7: spacing between the bars

subQuestions.label: 2.1.3 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the percentage increase in Kagiso Rabada's contract price (9,25 crore) from his base price (2 crore). Use: Percentage increase = ((new price − old price) ÷ old price) × 100%.

subQuestions.label: 2.2.1 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: A graph shows the value of $1 in rand over two days (28–30 March 2022), moving from a high of R14,6458 to R14,4701. Name the type of graph used to show the currency exchange rate.
subQuestions.memoText:
A broken-line graph (line graph).

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.label: 2.2.1 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: How would you describe the strength of the rand against the dollar over the time period shown? Use values and dates from the graph to help explain your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
The rand has strengthened: $1 fell from a high of R14,6458 to R14,4701 over the days 28–30 March. Fewer rand are needed to buy one dollar, which means the rand has become stronger.

Mark 1: 'strengthened'
Mark 2: high of R14,6458
Mark 3: down to R14,4701
Mark 4: dates 28–30 March

subQuestions.label: 2.2.1 (c)
subQuestions.questionText: Explain how this graph is misleading. Use values from the graph to support your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
The vertical axis does not start at zero — it starts at about R14,4482 — so the rises and falls look far more extreme than they really are. (Also: the line goes down, yet this actually represents the rand strengthening.)

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Brevis buys shares (in US dollars) at $1 = R14,4701: McDonald's 20 shares at $248,17; Nike 50 shares at $139,14; Netflix 30 shares at $391,82. Calculate, in rand, the total amount Brevis needs to purchase all these shares.

questions.title: Cell Phone Contracts — Fixed Costs, Probability, VAT and Comparing Tariff Graphs

subQuestions.questionText: Three iPhone 13 Mini contract options: Option 1 (Telkom) R700 per month × 24; Option 2 (Vodacom) R900 per month × 36; Option 3 (MTN) R950 per month × 3 years. Use the fixed monthly costs to determine the total fixed cost that will be paid for each of the three contracts.
subQuestions.memoText:
Option 1 = R700 × 24 = R16 800
Option 2 = R900 × 36 = R32 400
Option 3 = R950 × 36 = R34 200

Mark 1: Option 1 = R16 800
Mark 2: Option 2 = R32 400
Mark 3: R950 × 36
Mark 4: Option 3 = R34 200

subQuestions.questionText: Explain, without using the fixed monthly costs, which two factors will influence Brevis to choose one of the cell phone contracts.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any two of: the number of free minutes included per month; the call rate (cost per minute) for calls beyond the free minutes; the length of the contract.

[Award 2 marks per valid factor]

subQuestions.label: 3.1.3 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: If Brevis randomly chooses one of these three contracts, determine the probability that he would choose MTN. Give your answer to two decimal places.

subQuestions.label: 3.1.3 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the probability that he would choose Vodacom or Telkom. Give your answer to two decimal places.
subQuestions.memoText:
P(Vodacom or Telkom) = 2/3 = 0,67 (66,67%)

Mark 1: 2/3
Mark 2: 0,67

subQuestions.label: 3.1.4 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: The cash price of an iPhone 13 Mini is R15 500 inclusive of 15% VAT. Calculate the amount of VAT paid on the cash price of R15 500.

subQuestions.label: 3.1.4 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: What advice will you give Brevis to help him choose between paying cash (R15 500) or taking the Telkom monthly contract (R700 per month × 24)? Show all your calculations to motivate your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Cash price = R15 500
Telkom contract total (fixed) = R700 × 24 = R16 800
R15 500 < R16 800, a difference of R1 300.
Advise Brevis to pay cash — it is cheaper than the Telkom contract.

Mark 1: cash price R15 500
Mark 2: R700 × 24
Mark 3: contract total R16 800
Mark 4: conclusion — cash is cheaper

subQuestions.questionText:
Complete the missing values (a), (b) and (c) in the table.

Minutes: 0 | 10 | 25 | 50 | 100 | (c)
Total cost per month for Option 1 (Telkom): (a) | R700 | R700 | (b) | R820 | R980
Total cost per month for Option 2 (Vodacom): R900 | R900 | R900 | R900 | R900 | R980

(Telkom: R700 fixed, 25 free minutes, then R1,60 per minute.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) = Telkom cost at 0 minutes = R700 (within the 25 free minutes)
(b) = Telkom cost at 50 minutes = R700 + (50 − 25) × R1,60 = R700 + R40 = R740
(c) = minutes where Telkom cost = R980: (R980 − R700) ÷ R1,60 = 175 extra minutes; minutes = 175 + 25 = 200
(Check: Vodacom at 200 min = R900 + (200 − 100) × R0,80 = R980.)

Mark 1–2: (a) = R700
Mark 3–4: (b) = R740
Mark 5–6: (c) = 200 minutes

subQuestions.questionText: Using your completed table for Question 3.1.5, describe the two linear graphs you would draw on the same grid as Option 3 (MTN, already drawn), showing the relationship between the number of minutes used and the cost per month for Option 1 and Option 2.
subQuestions.memoText:
Heading (e.g. "Cost graphs of three cellphone companies") and axis labels (Number of minutes used per month; Cost in Rands).
Option 1 (Telkom): horizontal at R700 up to 25 minutes, then rising straight line through (50; 740), (100; 820), (200; 980).
Option 2 (Vodacom): horizontal at R900 up to 100 minutes, then rising to (200; 980).
Join points with a ruler; include a key.

Mark 1: heading and axis labels
Marks 2–4: plotting Option 1 points (from 3.1.5) correctly
Mark 5: plotting Option 2 correctly
Mark 6: joining with a ruler + key

subQuestions.label: 3.1.7 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: Write down the number of minutes and cost at which the cost for Option 1 (Telkom) and Option 3 (MTN) are the same.
subQuestions.memoText:
180 minutes; R950

Mark 1: 180 minutes
Mark 2: R950

subQuestions.label: 3.1.7 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine after how many call units the MTN contract becomes more economical when compared to the other two service providers.
subQuestions.memoText:
After 180 call minutes (units) the MTN contract becomes the more economical choice.

[Award 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: If Brevis uses more than 25 call minutes, but less than 180 call minutes per month, which contract would be the most cost-effective? Give a reason for your choice.
subQuestions.memoText:
Option 1 (Telkom) — its graph lies below the other two graphs in that range, so it is the cheapest of the three.

Mark 1: Option 1
Mark 2: reason (graph is below the others / it is the cheapest)

questions.title: Johannesburg Electricity Tariffs — Stepped Tariffs, Averages and a Stacked Bar Graph

subQuestions.questionText: The City of Johannesburg stepped tariff (2021/2022, including VAT): Block 1 (0–500 kwh) 146,48 c/kwh; Block 2 (501–1 000 kwh) 169,11 c/kwh; Block 3 (1 001–2 000 kwh) 182,07 c/kwh. Compulsory monthly charges: service charge 169,30 c; capacity charge 498,74 c. Sashin uses 1 100 units in January 2022 and calculates this to be R1 766,70 (including VAT). Using calculations, show he is correct.
subQuestions.memoText:
Block 1: 500 × 146,48 = 73 240 c
Block 2: 500 × 169,11 = 84 555 c
Block 3: 100 × 182,07 = 18 207 c   (1 100 − 1 000 = 100 units)
Subtotal = 73 240 + 84 555 + 18 207 = 176 002 c
Add fixed charges: 176 002 + 169,30 + 498,74 = 176 670,04 c
÷ 100 = R1 766,70 ✓

Mark 1: 500 units at Block 1 rate
Mark 2: 500 units at Block 2 rate
Mark 3: 100 units at Block 3 rate
Mark 4: adding the service charge (169,30)
Mark 5: adding the capacity charge (498,74)
Mark 6: ÷ 100 → R1 766,70

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate, in rand rounded to two decimal places, the average cost per unit for the 1 100 units of electricity consumed by Sashin for January 2022 (total R1 766,70).
subQuestions.memoText:
Average cost per unit = R1 766,70 ÷ 1 100 = R1,61 per unit

Mark 1: dividing the total by 1 100
Mark 2: correct value
Mark 3: written as a rate, R1,61 per unit

subQuestions.questionText: The 2021/2022 tariff table includes a 14,59% increase in electricity costs. Calculate how much Sashin would have paid for the same 1 100 units of electricity in the previous financial year (before the increase).
subQuestions.memoText:
Previous cost = R1 766,70 ÷ 114,59% = R1 766,70 ÷ 1,1459 = R1 541,76

Mark 1: dividing by 114,59% (1,1459)
Mark 2: correct value
Mark 3: rounding → R1 541,76

subQuestions.questionText: Use the step graph to complete the 2021/2022 tariff table. Block one (0–500 kwh) is done. Block two (501–1 000 kwh) = 146 c/kwh. Find: (a) the Block three tariff; (b) the kwh range for Block three; (c) the kwh range for Block five; (d) the Block five tariff.
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) ≈ 169 c/kwh
(b) 1 001–2 000 kwh
(c) 3 001 kwh or more (i.e. more than 3 000 kwh)
(d) ≈ 202 c/kwh

Mark 1: (a) 169
Mark 2: (b) 1 001–2 000 kwh
Mark 3–4: (c) 3 001 kwh or more
Mark 5: (d) 202

subQuestions.questionText: A stacked bar graph shows the Eskom average electricity price percentage increase versus the annual inflation rate of South Africa, by year. Determine the annual inflation rate during 2020.
subQuestions.memoText:
2%

[Award 2 marks for reading the graph]

subQuestions.questionText: The graph covers 27 years. In 4 of those years the annual price increase percent and the inflation rate percent were exactly the same. Calculate, as a percentage, the probability of randomly selecting a year in which they were exactly the same.
subQuestions.memoText:
P = 4 ÷ 27 × 100 = 14,8%

Mark 1: 4 (matching years)
Mark 2: ÷ 27
Mark 3: × 100
Mark 4: 14,8%

subQuestions.questionText: Determine the year which had the largest increase in the price of electricity. Write down the value of this percentage increase.
subQuestions.memoText:
2009, with a 31% increase.

Mark 1: 2009
Mark 2: 31%

subQuestions.questionText: Load-shedding was implemented for the first time in 2007. What effect, if any, did this have on the annual electricity price increase? Use values from the graph to support your view.
subQuestions.memoText:
After 2007 there were several sharp increases in the electricity price, all with increases of over 20% (for example 2009 at 31%, 2010 at 25%, 2011 at 26% and 2012 at 25%).

[Award marks for identifying the sharp post-2007 increases and citing values over 20%]

subQuestions.questionText: Sashin says that the higher the inflation rate increase, the higher the increase in electricity. Use dates and values from the graph to show that Sashin is incorrect.
subQuestions.memoText:
Counter-examples from the graph:
- In 2013 the inflation rate was 5% but the electricity price increase was 15% (low inflation, high price increase).
- In 2000 the inflation rate was 7% but the electricity price increase was only 1% (high inflation, low price increase).
So a higher inflation rate does not always mean a higher electricity price increase — Sashin is incorrect.

Mark 1: a low-inflation / high-increase year with values
Mark 2: a high-inflation / low-increase year with values
Mark 3: conclusion — Sashin is incorrect

questions.title: Wade Spears — Annual Salary, Pension, Income Tax and the Tax Threshold

subQuestions.questionText: Wade Spears is a 28-year-old teacher who earns R45 000 a month. Calculate his annual gross salary.
subQuestions.memoText:
Annual gross salary = R45 000 × 12 = R540 000

Mark 1: × 12
Mark 2: answer R540 000

subQuestions.questionText: Wade contributes 15% of his salary to his pension fund each month. Calculate his annual pension fund contribution.
subQuestions.memoText:
Annual pension = 15% × R540 000 = R81 000

Mark 1: 15% of R540 000
Mark 2: answer R81 000

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate Wade's annual taxable salary. Annual taxable salary = annual gross salary − annual pension contribution.
subQuestions.memoText:
Annual taxable salary = R540 000 − R81 000 = R459 000

Mark 1: subtracting R81 000
Mark 2: answer R459 000

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate Wade's tax for the year ending 28 February 2023. Tax table bracket R353 101 – R488 700: R73 726 + 31% of taxable income above R353 100. Primary rebate: R16 425. His annual taxable salary is R459 000.

The tax threshold for taxpayers under 65 years old is R91 250. Use the tax table (first bracket: 18% of taxable income; primary rebate R16 425), with calculations, to show how this amount was calculated.
subQuestions.memoText:
At the tax threshold, the tax payable is R0.
In the first bracket: 18% × threshold − R16 425 (rebate) = R0
So 18% × threshold = R16 425
Threshold = R16 425 ÷ 0,18 = R91 250 ✓

Mark 1: setting tax payable to R0 (18% × threshold = rebate)
Mark 2: R16 425 ÷ 0,18
Mark 3: answer R91 250
